subject: Post-demo: Hosting intent, migration preferences & lift-and-shift action items
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@acme-retail.com>, Lindsay Park <lindsay.park@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 09 Nov 2025 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: Hosting intent, migration preferences & lift-and-shift action items

Hi Samir / Lindsay —

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today. Quick recap from my side and a short set of asks so we can scope the migration path properly.

Highlights from the call:
- Primary objective: Replace current on-prem GPU cluster inference stack and reduce per-token cost while improving 99th-percentile latency for customer-facing suggestions.
- Current stack: mix of an older self-hosted Triton endpoint + a separate third-party LLM API for some embeddings.
- Main constraints: SOC2 evidence, network isolation for PII pipelines, and an internal procurement window in January.

Key clarification we need from your engineering/procurement team so we can propose a concrete plan:
1) Preferred serving mode (pick one for planning): Hosted API (fastest start), Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools in our cloud), or Private (VPC or on-prem bundle). If you have a strict requirement for customer-managed networking or HSM, call out Private.
2) Migration style: Lift-and-shift from current on-prem GPU cluster, hybrid (keep some workloads on your cluster + Redwood Dedicated for burst), or full cutover from the third-party API to Redwood Hosted.
3) Target cutover window and any immovable procurement deadlines.
4) Any model compatibility issues — are you tied to a specific model binary or do you want our recommendations (quantized variants supported)?

Proposed mutual action plan (attached: MAP_Acme_Retail_v1.pdf):
- Week 1: Confirm serving mode + representative traffic profile (qps, average seq len, p95/p99 targets).
- Week 2: Security review (SOC2 docs, network diagrams) + dedicated SE discovery to size capacity.
- Week 3-4: PoC with small traffic slice (256k tokens/day) using your existing model weights or our recommendation.
- Procurement: Redwood drafts SOW and pricing (if Dedicated or Private) — target draft by week 3.

Please reply with items 1–3 above and attach any existing architecture diagrams. If you prefer, Karthik can run a shorter technical sync next week to capture PCI/PII boundaries.

Thanks,
Rafael
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: MAP_Acme_Retail_v1.pdf, inference-hosting-options-comparison.xlsx

From: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@acme-retail.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lindsay Park <lindsay.park@acme-retail.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 09:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Hosting intent, migration preferences & lift-and-shift action items

Rafael —

Appreciate the concise summary. Short answers below:
1) Serving mode: leaning toward Dedicated capacity. We want predictable costs and isolation but don't have the bandwidth for a full Private on day one.
2) Migration style: preferred path is lift-and-shift for model scoring (we'll keep embeddings on the 3rd-party API during PoC), then a phased cutover for embeddings once latency and cost targets are met.
3) Cutover window: procurement committee meets first week of January — target contract signing by end of January, pilot in February.
4) Models: we use an in-house fine-tuned LLM exported as Hugging Face transformer weights; happy to have your SE evaluate compatibility.

I'll attach a short diagram of our current GPU farm (attached: acme_gpu_layout_v3.png). We're SOC2 Type II compliant but will need redwood SOC2 artifacts and any network diagram templates you use.

Thanks — will loop in procurement if we need to get Lindsay added to the MAP doc.

—Samir
Samir Gupta
Engineering Manager, Search & Recommendations
samir.gupta@acme-retail.com
+1 (212) 555-9932

Attachments: acme_gpu_layout_v3.png

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@acme-retail.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Hosting intent, migration preferences & lift-and-shift action items

Thanks Samir — this is great context. A couple of technical clarifications from the SE side so we size Dedicated correctly: 
- Can you confirm approx memory footprint of the largest model checkpoint (GB) and whether you expect kv-cache retention for long contexts (>8k tokens)?
- Which GPU types are in your current farm (A100 40GB / A100 80GB / T4 / V100)? If you have a short inventory that helps size the equivalent Dedicated pool.
- For the embedding flow you plan to keep on the 3rd-party API initially — are you concerned about cohesion (embedding drift) during phased cutover? We can run AB evals during PoC.

I can be flexible on timing; Rafael — if you want, I can schedule a 45-minute technical sizing call with Samir and their infra lead next Wed or Thu.

-Karthik
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Hosting intent, migration preferences & lift-and-shift action items

Looping in a quick CS checklist for the pilot and renewal cadence (putting dates here to keep momentum):
- By 11/17: Request for SOC2 artifacts and network diagram templates (we'll send).
- By 11/21: SE sizing call scheduled (Karthik to confirm date/time).
- By 12/05: Pilot plan drafted (traffic slice, rollback plan, success metrics).
- Procurement window flagged: Jan 5 meeting -> target SOW draft by 01/20 to give Acme 2 weeks to review.

Also noting: include a short paragraph in the SOW about model portability and fallback policies (Hosted fallback to smaller quantized model or Dedicated fallback to hosted variant). Procurement likes explicit fallbacks.

-Monica
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwoodinference.com
